newsitem.title: USA: US jobless rate under 5 pct possible this year - Reich.
newsitem.headline: US jobless rate under 5 pct possible this year - Reich.

text.p: An unemployment rate under five percent this year was possible, Labor Secretary Robert Reich said Wednesday.

"Many people were saying a year and a half ago that you couldn't possibly have unemployment that long under 5.5 percent without igniting inflation and yet we have done so," Reich told Reuters Financial Television.
"That's the way the economy is now organized, that's the structure of the economy, so anything is possible," he said when asked about a sub-five percent jobless rate.
The September jobless rate was 5.2 percent. October's employment data is due out on Friday.
Reich agreed that labor markets were tight but said Tuesday's employment cost index showed that wages and benefits were moving in tandem with inflation.

Wages had recently exceeded the rate of inflation but the cost of health benefits had slackened, allowing companies to pay higher wages without threatening to boost inflation. "That's good news all around," he said.
"There is undoubted tightening in labor markets," Reich added. Many employers across the country had told him they could not get the skilled workers they needed.
"My response - train your workers, go out and find people," he said, pointing out there were still 6.8 million people unemployed in the United States.
